full_judgment: 7. Mr.Habibul Islam Bhuiyan, the learned Senior Advocate appears on behalf of the petitioner while Mr. Shamsuddin Bulbul, the learned Advocate appears on behalf of the respondents. The learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the courts below failed to consider the evidence on record and arrived at erroneous conclusion. The learned Advocate further submits that the High Court Division failed to consider that the plaintiff purchased the suit land on 29.3.1990 from the defendant-petitioner and on the same date the plain-tiff executed and registered a deed of agreement with a condition that if the defendant paid back the said consideration money within 3 (three) months from the date of execution of sale deed. then _the plaintiff shall be bound to re-convey the suit land and thus Section 95A of the S.A. & T Act, 1950 any conditional sale will be treated as 'usufructuary mortgage and hence the impugned judgment of the High Court Division suffers from misconception of law The learned Advocate also submits that the 'High Court Division failed to appreciate the facts that the sale was conditional one with an agreement to re-convey and it constituted a usufructuary mortgage for which no suit for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession is maintainable.
